newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea to introduce market economy in trade zone.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea to introduce market economy in trade zone.

text.p: North Korea plans to introduce a market economy, including currency reform, to help liberalise a free economic and trade zone in the country, the domestic Joong-Ang Ilbo newspaper said in its Tuesday editions distributed on Monday.
The newspaper said it had obtained exclusive access to a report on an 11-point economic reform programme which Pyongyang had submitted to the U.N. Development Program (UNDP).

The programme for the Rajin-Sonbong free trade zone in the Tumen River Economic Development Area is believed to be the sweeping economic plans widely expected to be unveiled by Pyongyang in July, the daily said.
The programme includes abolishing a two-tier foreign exchange system in the zone, under which only special notes were convertible into foreign currency.
In line with the reforms, North Korea had made its existing currency convertible into dollars in the zone since June 1, the daily said.
The programme also allows workers and farmers self-management and to independently sell their products in such areas as foreign trade, transport, processing of farm products and restaurants.
North Korea also plans to expand the sea route between Rajin and Pusan in South Korea to Osaka next month, the daily said.
